toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__list_apps
toolsAdded.description:
List Linux apps — both currently running and installed-but-not-running — with per-app state flags:

- running: is a process for this app live? (pid is 0 when false)
- active: reserved (Linux X11/Wayland focus model differs from frontmost-app); always false.
- kind: `"desktop"` for XDG `.desktop` launcher entries.
- launch_path: the launcher command from `Exec=` (field codes stripped). Pass to `launch_app(launch_path=...)`.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__list_windows
toolsAdded.description: List top-level windows. Each record includes z_index (integer or null; higher values are closer to the front; null means stacking order is unavailable and callers must not infer one). To select a frontmost candidate, take the maximum integer z_index; if every value is null, use an explicit fallback instead of relying on array order. Filter with `app` or `pid`: an unfiltered call lists every window on the host.

app.description: Only windows of apps whose name contains this text (case-insensitive), or whose bundle id equals it.

on_screen_only.description: When true, filter to visible windows only. Default false.

pid.description: Only list windows owned by this process ID.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__get_window_state

Every actionable element is tagged `[N]` (an element_index); its element_token is `<snapshot_id>:N`, where `snapshot_id` is printed in the response header and returned in structuredContent. include_accessibility_tree.description: Default true — walk the AT-SPI tree and return it (per `tree_format`) alongside the screenshot.

include_screenshot.description: Default true — returns a grounding screenshot alongside the tree.

max_depth.description: Cap on the AT-SPI tree walk depth. Omit for the default (uncapped). Lower for deeply nested apps.

max_dimension.description: Legacy optional cap on the returned screenshot's long edge.

max_elements.description: Cap on total AT-SPI nodes walked. Default 250 (5 000 with full_output:true); the response states when the tree was cut.

pid.description: Process ID that owns the window.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring. Projects both tree_markdown and structured elements to matches plus ancestors while preserving original ...

since.description: A `snapshot_id` from an earlier get_window_state of the same window, or "latest" for this window's most recent read with the same query/max_ ...

tree_format.description: Which tree representation to return. Default "markdown": the compact `tree_markdown` only, where a row `[N]` is addressed with element_token ...

window_id.description: Native window identifier from list_windows, or the `popup.window_id` a click / right_click result named (an open context menu / popover; its ...

fresh.description: Force a new read even though nothing was done since the tree that came back with your last action.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__click
toolsAdded.description:
Click against a target pid. **Prefer `element_token` over pixel coordinates** — element_token works on backgrounded / hidden windows, surfaces a stable handle, and tells you what you're clicking via the cached AT-SPI element's role + label. Reach for `x, y` only when the target is a canvas / custom-drawn surface that doesn't appear in the AT-SPI tree.

Provide either (window_id + x/y) or (pid + element_token).

button.description: Mouse button. Default: "left" (legacy back-compat). X11: routed via ButtonPress/Release with the matching evdev code.

coordinate_frame.description: Frame of x/y (and from_x/from_y/to_x/to_y). Default "window": window-local screenshot pixels as returned by get_window_state.

count.description: Number of clicks in one press train: 1 (default), 2 = double-click, 3 = triple-click (line/paragraph selection).

element_token.description: Element handle `<snapshot_id>:<row>` from get_window_state: row `[11]` of a read whose snapshot_id is s0000002a is "s0000002a:11" (also in ` ...

modifier.description: Modifier keys held during the action: cmd, shift, option/alt, ctrl.

pid.description: Target process ID. Required unless scope is "desktop" or element_token is supplied (the token carries the pid).

window_id.description: Window id from list_windows. Required with x/y or element_index; optional with element_token (the token carries it).

x.description: Window-local pixel X of the target window's own get_window_state screenshot (0..screenshot_width).

y.description: Window-local pixel Y of the target window's own get_window_state screenshot (0..screenshot_height); see x.

gate_confirm.description: Confirmation code the gate gave for a high-risk action, only after the user approved it.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__request_human
toolsAdded.description: Ask the person at this computer. kind=approve: a yes/no on what you are about to do. kind=answer: a short free-text answer (e.g. which option they want). kind=takeover: ask them to do a step themselves (log in, solve a captcha, anything you cannot or should not do); it returns when they are done. Use only when a person is really needed.

question.description: What you need from them, in one or two plain sentences.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__run_actions
toolsAdded.description:
Batch mode: run several GUI steps in ONE call (single-step tools remain available). Each GUI step is checked by the gate like a single call. Steps, in order:
  {tool, args, expect?}  a GUI action (click, type_text, press_key, hotkey, scroll, set_value, ...). Name things that appear only after an earlier step with args.target = {label, role?}; the gate finds them on screen when the step runs. x/y only in the first GUI step.
  {find: SELECTOR, as: "rows", max?: 20}  read the screen now and keep the matching elements.
  {for_each: "rows", do: [steps]}  repeat steps per element; inside, args.target = "$item" points at it and "$item.label" in any string is its label.
  {if: {exists: SELECTOR} | {not_exists: SELECTOR}, then: [steps], else?: [steps]}
  {read: SELECTOR, as?: "name"}  report the matching elements' labels/values in the result.
SELECTOR = {label} exact, {label_contains}, {label_regex} and/or {role}. The batch stops at the first refused or failed step, when a dialog opens unexpectedly (a popup menu is fine), or when an expect fails ({title_contains} or {new_window: true}). You get what ran plus one fresh read of the window at the end. Max 20 GUI actions.

pid.description: Default pid for steps that omit it.

window_id.description: Default window_id for steps that omit it.

steps.description: The program, see the tool description.

List Linux apps — both currently running and installed-but-not-running — with per-app state flags:

toolsAdded.name: mcp__gui__run_actions
toolsAdded.description:
Batch mode: run several GUI steps in ONE call (single-step tools remain available). Each GUI step is checked by the gate like a single call. Steps, in order:
  {tool, args, expect?}  a GUI action (click, type_text, press_key, hotkey, scroll, set_value, ...). Name things that appear only after an earlier step with args.target = {label, role?}; the gate finds them on screen when the step runs. x/y only in the first GUI step.
  {find: SELECTOR, as: "rows", max?: 20}  read the screen now and keep the matching elements.
  {for_each: "rows", do: [steps]}  repeat steps per element; inside, args.target = "$item" points at it and "$item.label" in any string is its label.
  {if: {exists: SELECTOR} | {not_exists: SELECTOR}, then: [steps], else?: [steps]}
  {read: SELECTOR, as?: "name"}  report the matching elements' labels/values in the result.
SELECTOR = {label} exact, {label_contains}, {label_regex} and/or {role}. The batch stops at the first refused or failed step, when a dialog opens unexpectedly (a popup menu is fine), or when an expect fails ({title_contains} or {new_window: true}). You get what ran plus one fresh read of the window at the end. Max 20 GUI actions.

pid.description: Default pid for steps that omit it.

window_id.description: Default window_id for steps that omit it.

steps.description: The program, see the tool description.
